newsitem.title: CANADA: CP says shop moves to save C$10 mln/year.
newsitem.headline: CP says shop moves to save C$10 mln/year.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd unit CP Rail System confirmed on Thursday it was consolidating four of its repair shops into two locations in a move aimed at saving the company C$10 million a year.

The move "will result in heavy car and locomotive repair operations moving in early February 1997 from Weston Shops in Winnipeg to Ogden Shops in Calgary, while car repair operations currently performed in Sudbury will be moved to Thunder Bay," CP Rail said in a statement.
The compabny said 360 jobs would be affected by the restructuring -- 275 in Winnipeg and 85 in Sudbury.

CP said 137 positions were to be eliminated in Winnipeg, which is the site of the 700-employee Weston car shop, locomotive shop, component shop and support facilities. The remaining 138 repair staff would be transferred to Calgary.
The company said running or light repairs and routine maintenance to locomotives and cars would continue in Winnipeg and at two other facilities in the railway's main yard.
In Ontario, CP will close its Sudbury repair shop, which now employs 99, it said.
Of those jobs, 43 will be transferred to Thunder Bay and 42 eliminated. Fourteen repair workers will stay in Sudbury, the company said.

"The restructuring is part of a program which began in 1993 and is designed to streamline car and locomotive repair facilities and provide better shop and equipment utilization," CP Rail vice-president Neal Foot said in a statement.
